topic.label: Drones
topic.desc: Drones (uncrewed aircraft): platforms and makers, airframe types, applications, autopilots, payloads, regulation and mission data. Drones are aerial robots; the Robotics topic holds the shared control and navigation skills. Includes planetary and extreme-environment UAVs (Moon, Mars).

concepts: Makers of drones and autopilots, and the open flight-control stacks, compared from public specifications.
Multirotor, fixed-wing, VTOL and helicopter airframes and what each is suited to.
What drones are used for: survey and mapping, inspection, agriculture and similar work.
Autopilot configuration, flight modes, MAVLink and failsafes.
Cameras, gimbals, LiDAR and multispectral sensors carried by drones.
Airspace classes, operating rules, record keeping and risk assessment, which differ by country.
Planning waypoint missions and processing the imagery and logs they produce.
Unmanned aerial vehicles for the Moon, Mars and other places with little or no air: why propellers need an atmosphere, thruster-based flight, low gravity, dust and cold.
skills: Compares drone makers and platforms on published specifications, software support and update policy, and marks every claim with its source.
Compares open autopilot software such as PX4 and ArduPilot on supported vehicles, ground-station tools and licensing, from their documentation.
Chooses between multirotor, fixed-wing and VTOL for a task from range, payload, landing space and wind.
Estimates flight time and usable payload from mass, battery capacity and drag and states the assumptions.
Plans an aerial survey with altitude, image overlap and ground control for the accuracy the client needs.
Plans inspection flights for structures such as towers and roofs, with standoff distance, camera angles and what to record.
Plans crop-monitoring flights with a multispectral or visual camera and the index maps to produce afterwards.
Reviews autopilot parameters, flight modes and tuning for a vehicle and flags settings that need a test flight.
Connects a companion computer or software to a flight controller over MAVLink and tests the messages in simulation first.
Defines geofence, return-to-home and battery or link-loss failsafes and lists how each one should be tested.
Chooses a camera, lens and gimbal settings for a task and computes ground sample distance.
Matches LiDAR or multispectral sensors to a mapping or crop task and sets point density or band requirements.
Collects airspace class, restrictions and notice requirements for a location from official sources and flags that the pilot must confirm them with the aviation authority.
Keeps a flight log of aircraft, pilot, battery cycles and maintenance in the form an authority may ask for.
Writes a pre-flight risk assessment covering people, property, weather and equipment and lists the mitigation for each risk.
Builds a waypoint mission with altitude, speed, overlap and battery reserve and simulates it before upload.
Reads flight logs for vibration, battery sag, GPS quality and mode changes and explains anomalies.
Turns survey imagery into an orthomosaic, elevation model and point cloud and reports the accuracy against check points.

Decides whether an unmanned aircraft can fly on the Moon, Mars or another body from its gravity and atmosphere density: rotors and wings need air, so the airless Moon rules out propellers and calls for thrusters.
Designs a thruster-driven hopper or flying UAV for an airless world such as the Moon, with lunar gravity, propellant budget, landing legs and regolith dust that must not reach the engines.
Sizes rotors for the thin carbon dioxide air of Mars from gravity, air density and blade tip speed, with cold-night heating and a reference to the Ingenuity Mars helicopter.
